opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin on Source Code. Admin requires the Engineer role; as a non-owner, max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requests admin on Source Code. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full_time Analyst (max write for non-owner), while Security lists contractor with basic training (max read; write requires advanced training, admin never allowed). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive valid policy: contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. Admin is above the maximum, so grant the maximum of read.
